jobs.description:
Do you thrive in a dynamic environment where you can explore scientific challenges and have a significant impact? Are you passionate about developing life-saving vaccines, and enjoy close collaboration and leading a small development team?

We are expanding and looking for a new Manager to support our development projects!

**Join our team and let us make a difference together

**Our Process Development department in Hørsholm develops and optimizes vaccine production processes and supports our production sites. The Department handles diverse and evolving tasks and includes 32 members across 4 specialized teams.

We are looking for a manager to head our Drug Product Development and Analysis Team, consisting of three Scientists and three Technicians reporting to the Head of Process Development. The team focuses on drug product process and formulation development, stability studies, and analyzing development samples for ongoing programs.

Apart from managing the team an important part of the role will be hands-on to review analytical results, maintain the analytical methods and drive the execution of the analytical tasks in the team.

“We look forward to welcoming you to a dedicated and engaged department, where we value good team spirit and an easy-going, humorous environment,” says Janus Falhof, Head of Process Development.

**Your Impact

**You must have a strong interest in consistently delivering high-quality analytical data and to support the department’s development studies. Given the function of the team, there will be close interaction with all the teams in the department.

Your tasks will include:

• Driving the daily operation of the team, setting the scientific direction, and ensuring the development of the team members

• Ensuring established analysis assays run smoothly and deliver high-quality data on time, while supporting the team in developing new assays to advance the department

• Communicating daily with the team and collaborating closely with Production, Quality Control, and R&D

**Are You Our Next Pioneer?

**To succeed in this role, you will need the following qualifications:

• M.S. in Biotechnology, Human Biology, Biochemistry, Chemical Engineering, Pharmacy, or a related field, preferably with a PhD in protein chemistry or a related topic

• 3-5 years of relevant experience from the biotech industry or academia Previous experience with pharmaceutical analyses, e.g. chromatographic methods, particle methods and protein methods

• Previous experience with formulation development, statistical data analysis, and an understanding of protein chemistry

• Fluency in spoken and written English is required

**Who Are You?

**You are self-driven, responsible, and approach scientific challenges with curiosity and innovation. Success relies on strong teamwork, people skills, and the ability to engage in cross-functional dialogue. A proactive, calm, and positive attitude, combined with adaptability to new priorities, is beneficial. Good teamwork abilities are essential in a diverse, international department.

**Why join us?

**

• Be part of a team that directly contributes to global health by manufacturing and developing life-saving vaccines

• Your work here has a visible and significant impact, ensuring the safety and well-being of millions

• Join the fascinating field of vaccine production, where every day brings new challenges and opportunities to protect public health

• Enjoy a vibrant staff club that offers a variety of diverse, fun, and exciting events

**Are you ready to join us in our mission?

**If this sounds like the next step in your career, we would love to hear from you.

We look forward to receiving your application together with your CV. We are conducting interviews on an ongoing basis and encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

We kindly request that headhunters or recruitment agencies refrain from contacting us regarding this position.

Employees can meet up in SimCorp’s own very popular Friday bar and students throughout the house also meet up on a regular basis in their own community.

• Take part in continuous improvements of tools and processes on team and individual level.

• Understand requirements, discuss solutions, implement, and test the chose solutions

Most of the development is done in C#. While we have a broad range of tasks and experiments, a lot of focus is on APIs as well as on optimizing our test suite.

• Pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Finance or related field (last year of BSc or first year of MSc)

• Experience with C#/.NET framework or any other OOP language

As a person, you value:

• Continually looking for ways to improve what we do and how we do it

We have a lot of experienced colleagues, and you can always count on their expertise while working on your tasks.

**Competitive salary, bonus scheme, and pension are essential for any work agreement. However, at SimCorp, we believe we can offer more. Therefore, in addition to the traditional benefit scheme, we provide an excellent work-life balance: flexible work hours, a hybrid workplace model. On top of that, we have IP sprints; where you have 3 weeks per quarter to spend on mastering your skills as well as contributing to the company development. There is never just only one route - we practice an individual approach to professional development to support the direction you want to take.

Applicants are invited for a double degree PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Biological and Chemical Engineering programme. The position is available from 01 January 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

The position is part of the MSCA project TagTIC - Target mining for the development of therapeutics against pathogen-induced cancers, ID: 101311627, Call: HORIZON-MSCA-2025-DN-01-01. Project website: tagtic.eu

Note that this is a double degree PhD project within an MSCA Joint Doctorate. Under the currently planned arrangement, the candidate will work for approximately three years at TissueGnostics GmbH in Vienna, Austria, and one year at Aarhus University, Denmark.

Research area and project description:

Microbial infections are increasingly recognized as important contributors to cancer, but identifying the spatial tissue features and molecular signatures associated with infection-driven disease remains challenging. Integrating tissue imaging with spatial transcriptomics and microbiome information offers opportunities to characterize disease-associated patterns and improve biomarker discovery.

Consortium: This PhD postion is part of the interdisciplinary TagTIC consortium, which brings together expertise in microbiology, virology, oncology, immunology, medicinal chemistry, imaging, AI, and bioinformatics, with support from associated partners in biotech, diagnostics, and science communication. Its collaborative structure allows doctoral candidates to work within a network where discovery science, technology development, training, and societal impact are closely connected.

Project DC11: This PhD is part of the TagTIC consortium. It combines machine learning with image analysis to support precision oncology. The aim is to develop AI algorithms that integrate tissue imaging, spatial transcriptomics and microbiome data (multiomics) to identify biomarkers and predict disease progression.

Project description: For technical reasons, you must upload a project description. Please simply copy the project description above and upload it as a PDF in the application.

jobs.occupation: Research Assistants in Medical Robotics (Navigation & Control)
jobs.description:
The Department of Computer Science invites applications for one-year research assistant positions focused on developing innovative robot control and navigation techniques using simulation-based learning for medical robotic endoscope devices.

  Project Background
 This project addresses two critical challenges in the field of medical robotics to improve patient care through advanced simulation and control:

   	
• Image-Based Navigation: Creating reward functions for scoring navigation policies for medical robotic devices moving inside the human body, relying solely on image information and accounting for environment changes through interaction models. 	
• Soft Robot Control: Developing learning-based methods to control a soft robot endoscope via high-level navigation policies to perform clinical procedures inside the human body, including quality assessment of these methods during in-vivo interventions.   The successful candidates will join a multidisciplinary and collaborative team renowned for cutting-edge research in medical imaging and simulation technologies, operating within a global network across France, Germany, and Spain.

  Roles and Responsibilities
 The successful candidates will play a central role in the project’s technical and scientific success. While the level of autonomy will vary by position, both roles will share the following core responsibilities:

   	
• Technical Development & Implementation: Designing and implementing machine learning methods for motion planning and control. This includes integrating simulation-based learning frameworks and demonstrating the resulting systems on real robotic hardware and soft robot endoscopes. 	
• Research & Scientific Contribution: Contributing to the project’s core objectives by producing impactful research outputs. This includes writing high-quality papers for peer-reviewed journals and presenting findings at international conferences. 	
• Collaboration & Knowledge Exchange: Facilitating collaborations with industrial partners and academic collaborators to ensure that the developed methodologies are meaningful and translatable to real-world clinical practice. 	
• Professional Growth & Mentorship: Engaging in a high-growth research environment. The positions can be extendable and towards a PhD depending on the future funding status. The project has a trackrecord of landing members in top PhD program and faculty positions. 	
• Interdisciplinary Integration: Actively participating in team discussions and workshops to integrate expertise across medical imaging, physics simulation, and robotics control.   Profile
 We are looking for a highly motivated and enthusiastic scientist with the following competencies and experience:

  Essential experience and skills

   	
• MSc in the fields mentioned above. 	
• You have a strong foundation and track record in robotics simulation, robot control, computer vision and/or machine learning for physical systems. 	
• You are highgly experienced in numerical optimization algorithms, preferably applied to motion planning or reinforcement learning. Hands-on experience on real robots especially soft robot systems is a plus. 	
• Proficient scientific computing and programming (C++/Python) and experience with libraries such as PyTorch, JAX, Warp, Taichi, or ROS. 	
• Excellent communication skills and a high level of motivation to work in a multidisciplinary, international research environment.   Desireable experience and skills

   	
• Experience in publishing peer-reviewed research in top-tier robotics or AI venues. 	
• Familiarity with physics simulation such as MuJoCo, Isaac Sim, Newton Physics, SOFA etc.   Terms of employment
 The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week.

  The position is a fixed-term position limited to a period of 1 year. The starting date is 15 February or after agreement

  Salary, pension and other conditions of employment are set in accordance with the Agreement between the Ministry of Taxation and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant organisation.

  Foreign and Danish applicants may be eligible for tax reductions, if they hold a PhD degree and have not lived in Denmark the last 10 years.

  The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2025. 

  Questions
 Further information on the Department is linked at http://www.science.ku.dk/english/about-the-faculty/organisation/. Inquiries about the positions can be made to kenny@di.ku.dk and hayi@di.ku.dk.

  Application procedure

   	
• Your online application must be submitted in English by clicking ‘Apply now’ below. Furthermore, your application must include the following documents/attachments – all in PDF format 	
• Motivated letter of application (max. one page). 	
• CV incl. education, work/research experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position. 	
• A certified/signed copy of a Master of Science certificate. 	
• List of publications.   Deadline for applications: 30 November 2026, 23:59 GMT +1.
 We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process 
 After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the hiring committee. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment by an unbiased assessor. Once the assessment work has been completed each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself.

  You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/

  The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

   

  The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

jobs.occupation: PhD Project in Photonic Quantum Error Correction
jobs.description:
The Novo Nordisk Foundation Quantum Computing Programme (NQCP) is expanding its talented and international team to add to its cutting-edge quantum programme in the heart of Copenhagen, Denmark. At the Niels Bohr Institute, University of Copenhagen, we are running an international quantum computing programme, funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation, that drives research and innovations at multiple levels - from developing scalable quantum processor technologies to quantum algorithms and applications. The long-term mission of the programme is to develop fault-tolerant quantum computing hardware and quantum algorithms that solve life-science-relevant chemical and biological problems.

  NQCP invites applicants for a PhD fellowship on fault-tolerant photonic quantum computing with qudits and group surface codes.

  Start date 1 April 2027 or after agreement.

  The project
 Quantum computers promise to solve problems beyond the reach of conventional computers, but their fragile quantum states are easily disturbed by noise. Quantum error correction protects information against these errors. This project will explore new error-correction methods for quantum computers that use photons, the particles of light. In particular, it will investigate photonic qudits, which can carry information in more than two states, and a promising family of error-correcting codes called group surface codes.

  You will develop theoretical models and software to investigate how these codes can be implemented using photonic circuits. Through numerical simulations, you will study how well they protect information, how they allow computations to be performed reliably, and what resources they require. The aim is to identify approaches that could make large-scale photonic quantum computers more efficient. The work focuses on theory, programming and numerical simulation, while maintaining a close connection to photonic hardware. The project is supported by the Danish e-Infrastructure Consortium (DeiC).

  Who are we looking for?
 We are looking for a motivated candidate with a background in physics, quantum information, computer science, mathematics, photonics or a related field, and a strong interest in fault-tolerant quantum computing.

  Relevant qualifications include:

   	
• A solid foundation in quantum mechanics and quantum information. 	
• Strong programming skills, preferably in Python, and an interest in scientific software development and numerical methods. 	
• Knowledge of quantum error correction, quantum computing architectures, quantum optics or topological quantum codes. Experience in one or more of these areas is an advantage. 	
• Experience with numerical simulations, decoding algorithms or high-performance computing is an advantage. 	
• A curious mindset, the ability to work independently and collaboratively, and a structured approach to research. 	
• Good written and spoken English and strong communication skills.   Applicants are not expected to have prior experience in all aspects of the project. Relevant research projects, software contributions, publications and other professional activities will be considered in the assessment.

  Our group and research - and what do we offer?
 The group is part of the Niels Bohr Institute, University of Copenhagen. We are located in Copenhagen.We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in a dynamic and international research environment hosted by NQCP at. You will be part of the photonics research environment and collaborate closely with researchers working on quantum computing architectures, quantum error correction and photonic quantum technologies.

  Principal supervisor is Associate Professor Stefano Paesani, Niels Bohr Institute, stefano.paesani@nbi.ku.dk. The co-supervisor will be Professor Apoorv Tiwari at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU). The project will involve close collaboration between the two institutions, with regular joint supervision meetings and in-person visits.

  Joining NQCP now, you will get involved in a well-established and ambitious programme, which offers excellent opportunities to build a career in advancing quantum computing. We want to make Denmark a world leader in quantum research, and we hope to attract people from all over the world.

  Life in Denmark is supported by strong social services, including universal healthcare, free or subsidised language courses, paid parental leave, subsidised day care and excellent public schools. Our work culture is egalitarian and prioritises work-life balance. Copenhagen offers excellent infrastructure, extensive cycling networks, a thriving food scene, museums and access to beautiful natural surroundings.

  The PhD programme 
 Depending on your level of education, you can undertake the PhD programme as:

  Option A: A three year full-time study within the framework of the regular PhD programme (5+3 scheme), if you already have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s degree.

  Option B: An up to five year full-time study programme within the framework of the integrated MSc and PhD programme (the 3+5 scheme), if you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master´s degree – but you have an education equivalent to a Danish bachelors´s degree.

   Option A: Getting into a position on the regular PhD programme 

  Qualifications needed for the regular programme
 To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project, e.g. Physics For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Terms of employment in the regular programme 
 Employment as PhD fellow is full time and for maximum 3 years.

  Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure. 

  Appointment will be subject to a security clearance.

  You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

   Option B: Getting into a position on the integrated MSc and PhD programme

  Qualifications needed for the integrated MSc and PhD programme 

  If you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master´s degree, you might be qualified for the integrated MSc and PhD programme, if you have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish bachelor´s degree. Here you can find out, if that is relevant for you: General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database. 

  Terms of the integrated programme
 To be eligible for the integrated scholarship, you are (or are eligible to be) enrolled at one of the faculty’s master programmes in Physics.

  Students on the integrated programme will enroll as PhD students simultaneously with completing their enrollment in this MSc degree programme.

  The duration of the integrated programme is up to five years, and depends on the amount of credits that you have passed on your MSc programme. For further information about the study programme, please see: www.science.ku.dk/phd, “Study Structures”.

  Until the MSc degree is obtained, (when exactly two years of the full 3+5 programme remains), the grant will be paid partly in the form of 48 state education grant portions (in Danish: “SU-klip”) plus salary for work (teaching, supervision etc.) totalling a workload of 150 working hours per year.

  A PhD grant portion is currently (2026) DKK 7.426 before tax.
 
 When you have obtained the MSc degree, you will transfer to the salary-earning part of the scholarship for a period of two years. At that point, the terms of employment and payment will be according to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State (AC). The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

  Appointment will be subject to a security clearance.

   Responsibilities and tasks in both PhD programmes

   	
• Complete and pass the MSc education in accordance with the curriculum of the MSc programme  (ONLY when you are attending the integrated MSc and PhD programme) 	
• Carry through an independent research project under supervision    	
• Complete PhD courses corresponding to approx. 30 ECTS / ½ FTE 	
• Participate in active research environments, including a stay at another research institution, preferably abroad 	
• Teaching and knowledge dissemination activities 	
• Write scientific papers aimed at high-impact journals 	
• Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project   We are looking for the following qualifications:

   	
• Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD project. 	
• Relevant publications. 	
• Relevant work experience. 	
• Other relevant professional activities. 	
• Curious mind-set with a strong interest in Physics. 	
• Good language and communication skills. 	
• A structures approach to work.   Application and Assessment Procedure
 Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include: 

   	
• Motivated letter of application (max. one page) 	
• Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position 	
• Original diplomas for Bachelor of Science or Master of Science and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted. 	
• Publication list (if possible) 	
• Reference letters (if available)   When you will be affiliated with the University of Copenhagen or otherwise have access to their research, you may be required to undergo a background screening. The purpose is to protect the security and research integrity of the University of Copenhagen.

  The deadline for applications is 22 November 2026, 23:59 GMT +1.

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process 
 After deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment by an unbiased expert assessor. You are notified, whether you will be passed for assessment.

  The assessor will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the above mentioned research area, techniques, skills and other requirements. The assessor will conclude whether each applicant is qualified and, if so, for which of the two models. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessment. You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

  Questions
 For specific information about the PhD fellowship, please contact the principal supervisor.

  General information about PhD study at the Faculty of SCIENCE is available at the PhD School’s website: https://www.science.ku.dk/phd/.

   

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the surrounding community and invites all regardless of personal background to apply for the position.

Are you curious about energy trading and looking for a student job where you can put your analytical skills to work? Join our Regulatory Reporting team in Aalborg and get hands-on experience in a complex industry.

Your team

It's a complex field, with multiple market participants, extensive regulation, and an ever-changing trading business. We work to make sense of that complexity and ensure our reporting is accurate.

Your role

As our new Student Assistant, you'll help ensure the accuracy of our regulatory reporting. You'll work with transaction data, perform controls, and investigate discrepancies to help us meet our compliance obligations.

You'll also have the chance to improve existing processes and help develop new controls as our trading activities evolve. Along the way, you'll build an understanding of energy trading and the regulations behind it.

• Perform controls and reconcile transaction data to ensure accurate reporting.

• Investigate discrepancies, document findings, and help resolve issues.

• Understand the transactions and regulatory requirements behind the data.

• Are familiar with Excel.

• Maybe have experience reading XML data.

Ready to join us?
